title: Your own message
description:
Change the program so it prints exactly these three lines, then exits with code 0:

```
x86-64 assembly
runs on the metal.
No safety net!
```

Put all three lines in one `db` (a new line is the number 10), let `equ $ - label` work out the length, and print them with one `write` system call.

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
message: db     "Hello from assembly!", 10
length  equ     $ - message

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel message]
        mov     edx, length
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

solution.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
message: db     "x86-64 assembly", 10, "runs on the metal.", 10, "No safety net!", 10
length  equ     $ - message

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel message]
        mov     edx, length
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: One `db` holds all three lines: `"x86-64 assembly", 10, "runs on the metal.", 10, "No safety net!", 10`. Right after it, `length equ $ - message` counts every byte.
Then the same `write` and `exit` system calls as the lesson's program.
rules: Print with the write system call.
